newsitem.title: CHINA: HK in Taiwan trade pact without consulting China.
newsitem.headline: HK in Taiwan trade pact without consulting China.

text.p: Hong Kong said on Thursday it did not consult its masters in Beijing before signing a preliminary pact with Taiwan that indicated support for Taipei's membership in the World Trade Organisation (WTO).

"We have not consulted China on this and have not heard any objection from it," a spokeswoman for Hong Kong's Trade Department told Reuters. "We can handle the issue (on our own) under the Basic Law, which guarantees autonomy on trade and economic matters."
The Basic Law, the territory's post-handover constitution, says Hong Kong, can participate in international organisations and international trade agreements under the name "Hong Kong, China".

A statement by the government of the Hong Kong Special Autonomous Region (HKSAR), which has WTO membership status as a "customs territory", said the tentative agreement initialled in Tokyo on Tuesday completed bilateral talks on Taipei's WTO membership application.
"Both sides have initialled the schedules of concessions made by Chinese Taipei, subject to final verification by respective authorities," said the statement.
The Hong Kong Trade Department spokeswoman said the concessions included tariff cuts for goods and market access commitments for services, mainly in the financial sector.
Both sides would confirm technical details before signing a formal agreement, she said.
Beijing, which resumed control over Hong Kong after its 156 years as a British colony, has vowed to allow it a high degree of autonomy.
Beijing also has said there should be no change in Taiwan's huge business ties with Hong Kong, which serves as a gateway for large Taiwan investment flows into China.
But it nonetheless requires that Hong Kong-Taiwan contacts be vetted by the communist government, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
Beijing has said it would accept Taiwan's membership in the WTO as a customs territory, but not before China itself gets in as the sole sovereign Chinese member.
The spokeswoman said Hong Kong has always supported Taiwan's membership in the international trade grouping.

"We support Chinese Taipei's entry into WTO provided it can carry out its obligations as a WTO member, abide by WTO rules and provide members with a meaningful market access commitment," she said. "This has always been our position, and we hold the same position to the entry of any applicant."
In 1990, Taiwan applied to join the WTO's predecessor, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, as a customs territory under the name of Chinese Taipei.
Under WTO accession rules, members are allowed to seek bilateral talks with applicants to negotiate what they regard as acceptable trade relations, including market access.
An agreement reached in these bilateral talks implies that the WTO member, for its part, has no objections to the applicant's bid to join.

"We are satisfied with the concessions made by Chinese Taipei," the Hong Kong government statement said. "The overall package has met our objective of securing meaningful market access commitments in respect of projects of significant export interests to the HKSAR and in the financial services sector."
